Depression is something I've dealt with my entire life. I've always managed to get through it relatively well on my own, up until a couple of months ago. Back around August, I had a severe bout of depression-- the worst I'd ever had. I could barely get out of bed for a week straight except when I really, really, really had to use the washroom. Every day became a fight to survive. Where normally I could stave off my depressive thoughts by weighing the pros and cons of certain obvious actions, I quickly found myself with only one con: I couldn't figure out how to make things "not messy" so I didn't disrupt too many peoples' day or greatly inconvenience whoever had to do the cleanup.

The circumstances around this bout were that I had just moved to the city and was thrust into a government employment program that returned me to school with the hope of getting a new career. The bout of depression led to my missing six days of school, and needless to say, my employment agent didn't like that very much. That was when I made the mistake of telling her that I had gone through a severely depressive period. I asked her for help. Her response was to pull me out of school and tell me that i wouldn't be allowed to get back in to the government program without a written letter from a psychologist or social worker saying that I could "handle" being in school.

Now, to a degree, I can understand her reasoning. The problem with her solution, though, was the same problem that had acted as a catalyst to my depression: I was feeling isolated. All my friends were in different cities. The one friend I did have in the area-- someone I grew up with-- ended up conning me out of nearly $2000. On top of it, as juvenile as it sounds, I was just learning how to make friends again at school. And now that had been taken away, too-- all because I had let people know what was going on with me. All because I was trying to ask for help.

I didn't learn any lessons that day. Instead, all the previous lessons I had learned in life reinforced one simple rule: do not ever ask for help. If you ask for help, things will get worse. People will seemingly go out of their way to make sure things get worse. You'll think you don't have anything to lose, but you do. And you will be in danger of losing whatever little you have left.
